blind.why: Enemy at 15 m in a real match (seed 2 B Connector vs ss_18). Ours pops because of its cyan emissive, which is better than CS2 for spotting. But the figure is a stiff idle block with no weight. CS2's shooter has a grounded stance, recoil and a muzzle read, so it reads as a person in combat.

Teammates seen from behind at 15 m (seed 3, Ember Spawn toward Mid vs t1_010). CS2's players have natural weight and gait. Our four figures stand with upper arms abducted to shoulder height ('chicken wings'). The sunlit Ember figure goes tan-orange against the tan/terracotta wall, while Tide pops.

Running enemy at 6 m (follow cam, seed 6 B site vs t2_027). Our stride is real, but the torso stays bolt upright, the arms are frozen and the pistol is held out one-handed at the chest. CS2's runner leans, swings and carries momentum.

biggest_gap: Ember still camouflages at range on this warm map. Repro: ?test=1&seed=3&match=1&phase=live, advance(6), set ctx.ai.enabled=false, put 2 Ember and 2 Tide at (-0.2,0,44.2) facing +z… then place the camera 30 m and 50 m down the line toward Mid (place(1.6,0,-5.8, yaw toward them)). Shots: shots/critic-avatars-r3/L3v1_30m.png, L3v1_50m.png and crops_line2.png. Tide reads instantly as cyan. The sunlit Ember turns into a tan-orange smudge on the sandstone, and the shaded Ember disappears into the terracotta wall. The cause is the suit colour: uSuit #934420–#a55018 is the same rust/terracotta hue and value family as the map's roofs and walls, so the orange bands sit on an orange background. Fix: push the Ember base to a true dark value (umber/charcoal, luminance ≤ 0.06, e.g. #3a2418) and keep orange only on the emissive bands, OR give Ember a non-map colour cue such as a bright light-cream/yellow helmet or visor band that survives at 50 m. Then re-verify ≥ 3:1 against both the sandstone (#d9b98a) and the terracotta (#b5552e) at 30 m and 50 m, in sun and in shade. CS2 keeps each side's value family distinct from the map palette.
other_gaps: Every weapon hold (pistol, rifle, run, crouch, plant) raises the upper arms close to horizontal and flares the elbows out to the sides. This makes a wide T-shaped 'chicken wing' silhouette that is clearest from behind (cs/sheet_pistol.png, cs/sheet_run.png). Drop the elbows: keep the upper arms about 30–45° from the torso, with the support elbow under the gun the way CS2 holds a rifle.

Hitboxes lead the drawn body on moving actors. Measured on runners at about 7 m/s (seed 4, side-on ray grid at 4 cm, hb2.log): capsule centroid sits 6–10 cm ahead of the mesh along velocity, the model root trails actor.pos by 5.8 cm, and about 20% of rays are mesh-only or box-only. The trailing visible edge cannot be hit. Evaluate the capsules at the rendered (interpolated) pose, or lag-compensate.

The locomotion torso is rigid: no forward lean at a run, no counter-rotation, no arm or weapon sway, no head bob, and the bot stays mid-stride while jumping over crates (run6_strip.png). Add lean that scales with speed, pelvis/chest counter-twist, and a jump/fall pose.

Body proportions are stacked boxes. The thighs and hips are as wide as the shoulders, there is no waist taper, the hands are huge black blocks and the guns look toy-sized next to the hands. It reads as a robot, not an athlete. Taper the thighs and waist, shrink the hands and enlarge the held weapon.

The plant pose is a deep knock-kneed squat with the beacon held at the crotch, not a kneel-and-place. In the throw sheet the canister sits at the hip for the sampled window, and the side view shows a plank-stiff lean.
Tide's teal suit lowers contrast against the map's many teal crates and floor decals (run6_f1.png). The emissive strips carry the read, so keep them strong.
bugs: Hitbox and render-pose mismatch on moving actors: 6–10 cm lead along velocity, and the root trails sim pos by about 1 tick.
A small magenta quad floats at the right hip of an Ember bot (seed 5, s5_ember2_5m.png). It could be a stray charm or a utility mesh.
strengths: Every colour slot is now locked per team: no opposite-team hues across all 10 actors in seed 7.
One skinned body draw per actor: about 4.3 calls and 5k tris per actor including shadow (43 calls for the cast).
The tag-out freeze-to-crystal then shatter reads clearly in a live match.
There is a visible stride cycle and crouch-walk foot lift.
